results.content:
Take the following actions:

 Use the keyboard with a local machine to determine whether there's an issue with the keyboard hardware.
 Verify that you have the latest WorkSpaces client.
 Reboot the WorkSpace from the WorkSpaces console.
 Turn off secure keyboard features in your antivirus software settings.  
   Note: Review the documentation for your antivirus software for instructions.
 Turn off custom key remapping applications.
 If you use an international keyboard, then verify that the keyboard layout on the WorkSpace and the client match. For Windows, see Manage the input and display language settings in Windows 10 on the Microsoft website. For macOS, see Type in another language on your Mac with input sources on the Apple website. [...] If your keyboard still doesn't respond, then complete the following steps:

1. Open the Keyboard Event Viewer in a web browser. See the Keyboard Event Viewer on the GitHub website.
2. Test each key of your keyboard. After you finished, leave the window open.
3. Log in to your WorkSpace.
4. Open the Keyboard Event Viewer in your WorkSpace.
5. Test each key of your keyboard.
6. Compare the key code in your WorkSpace to the key code in your web browser.

If the key codes are different, then you can change the keyboard layout so that both versions match. For more information, see Language and keyboard settings for WorkSpaces.

results.content: It Is What It Is. It Is What It Is AWS,OS X,Workspaces AWS Workspaces Keyboard on Mac. # AWS Workspaces Keyboard on Mac. Recently, I set up an AWS Workspace configuration for a client. I ran into an interestingly frustrating issue. When I launched the Workspace client from my Mac (macOS Sierra) the mouse would work just fine, but no keyboard input would be sent across. I spent a bit of time Googling and reading the developer forums, which selected quite a few possibilities, which I tried. Like many folks out there, none of the fixes presented solved my problem. I did, however, run across one post that mentioned programs that can change your key mappings, which now seemed like the most likely suspect to me. However, to my knowledge, I don’t have anything like that installed. I had a few likely suspects that I was not excited to try and test out the fix on, mostly because it would involve uninstalling them (Parallels, VirtualBox, etc). I decided to start with my AntiVirus – WebRoot. As it turns out, WebRoot includes a “Secure Keyboard Mode” under Advanced Settings. I disabled Secure Keyboard Mode and Amazon Workspaces immediately started accepting keyboard input from my Mac. My follow up advice on this is to only disable this setting when you are using Workspaces. Turn it back on, whenever you are done. A little frustrating, but WebRoot will be constantly alerting you that you are not secure if you don’t. ### Related Post. ## Sharing Private DNS between VPCs with Route53Sharing Private DNS between VPCs with Route53. results.content: Proceed by trial and error. Try another keyboard; for hardware problems it is not so significant that keyboard worked before: all things worked before breaking... If problem disappears, try cleaning the old keyboard. _Crumbs_ under the keys may prevent proper functioning. Check for contacts under problematic keys partially worn out. In case of different timing for catching keyboard interrupt between host and emulated OS. Emulated... have you tried if the problem occurs even if you work directly under Linux (with a system on USB)?
